title: Rabbi Yosi bar Asyan (or Yasinia)

paragraphs: Rabbi Yose bar Asyan, or Yasinia.

In Eruvin 53b they say: when Rabbi Yose bar Asyan spoke cryptically, he said, “Make me an ox in judgment on a poor mountain.” When asking about lodging, he said, “Man, mouth, this, living—what good is there?” In Beitzah 8b: “Rabbi Yose bar Yasinia (in Dikdukei Soferim: Yasyan) said: this applies only where he cannot cover it,” etc. (This refers to Rabbi Zeira’s statement.) Possibly he is Yose bar Ashyan, mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 4:6 as speaking in the name of Resh Lakish. In Ha-Asif 5648, p. 189, the author proposes that this Rabbi Yose ben Asyan is the Rabbi Yose mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 3:5: “Rabbi Yonah and Rabbi Yose permitted baking for Ursicinus on Shabbat.” Hyman rejects this as an error: as is known, Rabbi Yonah’s colleague was Rabbi Yose bar Zevida, who was indeed among the leading halakhic authorities, whereas Rabbi Yose bar Asyan is not found issuing halakhic rulings. “This is clear,” he concludes.

notes.text: Rashi on Eruvin53b decodes tor+din as teradin, beets, and har+dal as hardal, mustard. The lodging question likewise uses syllabic substitutions: Rashi and Tosafot (citing Rabbenu Chananel) give slightly different analyses. The literal riddle is retained rather than treating its words as place names.

Asyan/Yasinia/Yasyan/Ashyan are Hyman’s supplied name variants. The named Guggenheimer Sanhedrin3:5 paragraph confirms baking for Ursicinus; Hyman’s competing identification of the speaker remains his argument.

The inspected Rashi on Eruvin 53b decodes tor plus din as teradin, beets, and har plus dal as hardal, mustard. Rashi’s lodging analysis differs from Tosafot’s quotation of Rabbenu Chananel. Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 4:6 directly has Yose bar Ashyan reporting Resh Lakish; that occurrence does not establish the proposed identity. Hyman’s Ha-Asif criticism, certainty and halakhic-authority argument remain his; the exact Dikdukei Soferim and Ha-Asif editions were not inspected.
